41.20.0.en: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth [21].

41.20.1.en: The same poetic description is used when speaking of the wrath of God (Ps 18:8).

41.20.2.en: * What is this that he calls coals but the minds of corrupt men, kindled with earthly passions? They are on fire when they seek any temporal thing, surely because their longings, which do not allow their minds to be calm and balanced, inflame them. The breath of leviathan kindles the coals when his secret suggestions strengthen the minds of men toward evil pleasures.

41.20.3.en: His breath has kindled some with the torches of pride, others with envy, others with lust, and others with covetousness. He kindled the torch of pride in the mind of Eve, when he suggested to her that she should make light of the words of the Lord's commandment. And he set the mind of Cain on fire with the flame of envy when he was grieved at the acceptance of his brother's sacrifice, until he reached the sin of murdering his brother. He set the heart of Solomon on fire with the torches of lust, he whom he overcame by the love of women, and they led him to idolatry, and he forgot to give due honor to his Creator when the pleasures of the flesh drew him. He also inflamed the mind of Ahab with the love of covetousness when he urged him, in haste, to seek another's vineyard, and this drove him to the crime of murder.

41.20.4.en: The flame of the mouth is truly the very making of a secret suggestion.

41.21.0.en: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him [22].

41.21.1.en: "In his neck remaineth strength," that is, strength dwells there continually. While strength rests around his neck, since he breathes out terror, terror rejoices and dances with delight before him, spreading trembling upon those around him.

41.21.2.en: * We understand from these words that there is one King, who is the Creator of the whole universe. On the other side there is the prince of this world, who calls himself the king of darkness. Myriads of angels serve the true King, while myriads of demons surround the prince of the powers of darkness (Col 1:13). The principalities and powers and virtue follow the King of kings and Lord of lords. And in the end, when Christ delivers up the kingdom to God the Father, after He has put down all rule and all authority and power of the enemy, it is necessary that He reign till He has put all enemies under His feet (1 Cor 15:24-25).

41.21.3.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * What does the neck of this leviathan mean but the stretching out of his pride, whereby he exalts himself against God, while pretending holiness, as he is puffed up with the pride of authority? The prophet Isaiah bears witness to this pride, expressed by the neck, when he rebuked the daughters of Jerusalem, saying: "They walk with stretched forth necks" (Isa 3:16). It is said that strength remains (abides) in the neck of this leviathan, and because of the authority that has been added to his pride. For he continues his exalted pride and all his wicked plans by the power of his temporal authority.

41.21.5.en: * By such words (Jn 12:31; 14:30; 16:11) He refers to Satan as a prince not over God's creatures, but over sinners, those whom He here indicates by the name "this world." When He uses the name "world" in the sense of evil, the Lord refers only to the lovers of this world, of whom it is written elsewhere: [The friendship of the world is enmity with God] (Jas 4:4). Far be it from us to understand Satan as the prince of the world in the sense of one who controls the management of the affairs of the whole world, heaven and earth and all that is in them. Of such a world it was said when we spoke of Christ the Word: "The world was made by him" (Jn 1:10). The whole world, from the highest heavens to the lowest parts of the earth, is subject to the Creator, not to the fugitive; to the Savior, not to the destroyer; to the Deliverer, not to the enslaver; to the Teacher, not to the deceiver.

41.21.6.en: *But the prince of this world (Satan), who rules wherever there is error and confusion, departs from a man whose life is ruled by peace and perfect order, and over whom the Son of God has dominion. When this peace arises from within and is established, all the persecutions that the prince of this world stirs up from without cannot shake anything of that inner building; rather, the strength of the building from within causes the plots of the devil from without to fail. Therefore the Lord went on to say: "Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."

41.21.7.en: * "For either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon." Whoever serves mammon serves Satan, whom our Lord called (the prince of this world), because of his dominion by his error over earthly things. So a man will either "hate" this one "and love the other," that is, God, or hold to the one, "Satan," and despise the other, "God." For he who serves mammon is subject to the cruel and destructive Satan. For when he is entangled by his lust for money he submits to Satan and clings to him though he does not love him, for who among us loves Satan?! And so he is like a man who loved a maidservant of a great person, and though he does not love her master he submits to his cruel slavery because of his love for the maidservant.

41.22.0.en: St. Augustine The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved [23].

41.22.1.en: Usually the layers of flesh at the neck and at the belly are soft and weak, but in this animal the layers of flesh at his neck are joined together, molded as of iron, strong.

41.22.2.en: What a hideous picture! Just as the body of Christ grows to include every day souls that enjoy the righteousness and holiness of Christ and become partners with Him in glory, so also the body of the devil grows to include those who are more wicked than the former, and all are joined together like the joined flakes of the devil's flesh, as if they had become one mass like iron molded together, unmoved toward repentance and return to God. The union of the wicked together corrupts souls, and shuts the door before many from thinking seriously about enjoying the divine truth.

41.22.3.en: If the Lord Christ has joined us to Himself to be members of His one body, by our enjoying faith in Him, and our being born of the Spirit as children of God in the waters of Baptism, our mission is to join together in love every day those who are saved and who enjoy with us fellowship with Him in the new risen life which He gave us. So also the flakes of the body of Satan are those who have accepted sonship to him and are united with him through his works, and they do not cease to draw many with them to be members in the body of the devil, sharing his final fate even more than they do; for the wicked man is pleased when he joins with him one who becomes more wicked than himself.

41.22.4.en: * The body of leviathan (the wicked indeed) is wholly corrupt, for they have no longing for their spiritual city. The flakes of the body of leviathan are those who join these persons in a wicked life, and even outstrip the former in the way of evil... In the wicked company of this leviathan, these are the members of his body who by their wicked deeds join to him those whom they make more wicked than themselves.

41.23.0.en: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone [24].

41.23.1.en: The Lord Christ says: "God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham" (Mt 3:9). What are these stones that give children to Abraham but the idolaters, who worship stone, and the sons of the devil who bear his hard, stony heart (Job 41:24), that they may become children of God bearing the faith of Abraham.

41.23.2.en: Some hold that the huge predatory animals have weak feelings and a hard heart, if the expression is right, and care nothing for the cries of the prey and the blood shed from it while it is between their fangs.

41.23.3.en: He chooses here the lower millstone, because it must be harder and heavier than the upper stone, so that it may bear the motion of the upper stone and its pressure upon it.

41.23.4.en: Perhaps some will ask: Is Satan not given the joy of repenting? Since his fall he has not only been determined to resist God, but has increased in violence in his attitude, and even stirs up mankind to be like him, and to share in his violence and hardness of heart; so with time the cup of his evil is filled the more, and he cares nothing for eternal punishment, but finds his pleasure in the children of men sharing this fate with him.

41.23.5.en: * The heart of the ancient enemy will remain like a stone, for it will not be softened by any remorse of repentance. It will only be prepared for the blasts of eternal punishment.

41.23.7.en: * He is violent, knows no pity, and cannot be calmed in heart. As Holy Scripture says of him: "His heart is hard as a stone, and he stands like an anvil that is not struck" (Job 41:24) LXX. But Christ puts him under the feet of the saints. He says: "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you" (Lk 10:19).

41.23.8.en: St. Cyril the Great * So also Satan transforms himself into the form of an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), not in order to ascend again to where he was, for his heart is hard as an anvil, so that his will has become incapable of repenting. But he does this with the intention of plunging those who walk in an angelic life into the darkness of blindness and deadly unbelief.

41.23.9.en: Many wolves go about in sheep's clothing (Mt 7:15), yes, their clothes are sheep's clothing, but not their hooves or their teeth. And as they walk in the soft skin they deceive the innocent by their appearance, and pour into them from their fangs the poison of deadly defilement.

41.23.10.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * I will declare with confidence that there is one who is not much affected by [the hammer of the whole earth]. And since the example has been given of a hammer that can be perceived, look for a material stronger than the hammer which is not affected by its blows. By searching for it I found it in what is written: "Behold a man standing upon walls of adamant" (adamant: a hard stone which was thought to be uncuttable, and some thought it to be the diamond). History records of adamant that it is stronger than every hammer that strikes it, for it will neither break nor yield. Even if the hammer is the devil who stands upon it, and the serpent who with his unconquerable anvil places it under him, yet the adamant is not affected at all when it rests in the hand of God and under His care. Thus those who oppose the adamant are the hammer and the immovable anvil. However, there is in truth a very common proverb among the Gentiles in the common language concerning those who suffer from troubles and very difficult circumstances. They say: They are between the hammer and the anvil. Yet it can be said that this refers to Satan and the serpent, who are always meant by such two names in the Holy Scriptures for different purposes. And you can say that the holy person who is an adamant wall, or who is an adamant in the hand of the Lord, is affected neither by the hammer nor by the anvil, but the more he is struck the more the brightness of his shining virtue increases.

41.23.11.en: * He says: "Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall of adamant, and in his hand was an adamant" (Amos 7:7) LXX. If Satan is a hard hammer from above and the dragon like the hard anvil (Job 41:15) stands from below, then he who is in the hand of the Lord and under His protection is hard and never yields. For the holy man is an adamant wall, and as he remains in the hands of the Lord he suffers nothing even if he is placed between the hammer (the devil) and the dragon (the anvil). And the more the blows fall upon him, the more his virtue becomes bright. For Satan, being ignorant of this kind of rock (the adamant), wants to break it up by many blows like a hard hammer, but God alone knows their nature well.

41.23.12.en: Origen When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid.

41.24.0.en: By reason of terrors they wander [25].

41.24.1.en: When he rises to attack or to defend himself, the mighty are terrified before him, and from fear their thoughts collapse and they wander, or lose the way. They try to flee from him and do not know where to go.

41.25.0.en: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart (javelin), nor the habergeon [26].

41.25.1.en: The sword cannot overtake him, for it cannot break his scales. And if spears are aimed at him they rebound without piercing his scales.

41.25.2.en: * The spear of holy preaching is gentle; when we are struck by it we die to sin. But the sword of the satanic call is wicked; by it a man is wounded with deadly wounds until he is deprived of uprightness of life...

41.26.0.en: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood [27].

41.26.1.en: By iron and brass he means the metal weapons used against him; they are like straw and wood and worms, without power.

41.26.2.en: What occupies the devil's mind is not his bitter fate, but how to draw the souls of men to evil, especially the souls of believers; if he sees a soul strong as iron and hard as brass, he directs the arrows of his evil until the iron is turned into straw (chaff), and the brass into a feeble piece of wood. The enemy concentrates his blows the more on the preachers and witnesses to the evangelical truth, and those who labor in the Lord's vineyard.

41.26.3.en: * When this leviathan takes that sword which the Holy Scriptures call "the antichrist" to practice his evil, he turns iron into straw and brass into wood, unless divine grace intervenes to give protection from him, lest he turn the strength of the preachers into straw and destroy them with the fire of his evil, and make them like dust by turning their patience into wood.

41.26.5.en: The arrow cannot make him flee.

41.27.0.en: Slingstones are turned with him into stubble [28].

41.27.1.en: We can interpret this passage as relating to the believer: if the enemy of good spares no effort to urge believers to evil, and his battle against the Church of Christ never ceases, the believer for his part does not fear these satanic wars so long as he is sheltered by the Lord Christ, bearing the weapon of living faith. He is not terrified by the arrows of the devil's bow, nor by the stones, for the stones of his sling, which become like straw, will do him no harm.

41.27.2.en: * If you say that the opposing power is very strong, and that evil has complete mastery over man, you thereby attribute injustice to God when He condemns men for being subject to Satan, since Satan is very strong and subdues mankind with an irresistible power. By this you make Satan greater and stronger than the soul, and then you tell me not to submit to Satan. This is like a fight between a young man and a little child, in which the child, when defeated, is condemned for his defeat. This is a great injustice!

41.27.3.en: St. Macarius the Great * Do not fear Satan, then, even though he is without a body, when he approaches the body. For there is none weaker than he who approaches in this way, although he is not clothed with a body, and none stronger than that bold, courageous man, even though he bears a mortal body!

41.28.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear [29].

41.28.1.en: No tool or weapon can wound the crocodile, nor can any human power overtake it.

41.28.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that this passage applies to the devil, whom the Lord rebukes and reproves, as if he were being struck with a hammer; but in persistence in his evil he cares nothing for the blows of the hammer, but counts them as straw, and even laughs in mockery at these blows.

41.28.3.en: This applies also to the wicked who stubbornly hold to their evils, for God permits their chastening, that perhaps they may return to Him, but these blows with the hammer of chastening become to them like straw, and they do not return to the divine truth. Like their wicked master, the devil, they care nothing for the shaking of the divine spear to chasten them.

41.28.4.en: * The Lord shakes the spear against leviathan, for He threatens him with a harsh judgment for his destruction. For the shaking of the spear is the preparation of eternal death for him with a severe punishment. But the stubborn spirit, despising the Creator of life, even while he is threatened with his death laughs at Him who shakes the spear. Whatever his foreknowledge of his terrible, cruel fate drawing near to him with a firm sentence, he does not fear its coming upon him. Rather, the more he realizes that he is unable to escape the eternal torments, the more violently he increases in the practice of evil.

41.28.6.en: Again, as this passage applies to the true believer, the enemy of good who wants to put him on the anvil and strike him with the hammer, shapes him according to his own desire; God does not restrain the hammer, and permits him to put him on the anvil, but the blows of the hammer are turned into worthless straw, with no effect on the mind and life of the believer.

41.28.7.en: God does not prevent the trials and allurements of Satan, but gives His believers strength, so the trials are turned to nothing, and the believer gains victory and a crown.

41.29.0.en: He spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire [30].

41.29.1.en: Perhaps he refers here to sharp and hard scales like sharp pieces of potsherd. In some parts of the crocodile's body there are sharp scales, so that even when it rests on the mud found on the bank of the river it is like one resting on the teeth of a sharp threshing sledge. Perhaps he means that when it rests on sharp pieces of rock or jagged stones it feels no weariness or harm from them, but is as if it were resting on mud. Some scholars hold that when spears and other weapons are aimed around it they are broken and scattered around it, like sharp pieces of potsherd cast around it. Others hold that if this animal rests on mud, when it leaves the place it leaves the marks of its scales as if weapons had left their marks on the mud.

41.30.0.en: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment [31].

41.30.1.en: By his swift movement under the water he makes the river or the sea like a boiling pot. He makes the sea like a vessel containing perfumes; here is a reference to the smell of musk which, as they thought, comes from the crocodile. Some hold that when he moves vigorously in the depths of the sea he stirs up the mud in it, just as a man stirs a vessel of perfume so that the fragrance may be carried up from the sediment in the vessel.

41.30.2.en: The word "sea" here refers to the river Nile, because of its breadth, for to this day it is called in many regions of Upper Egypt "the sea." It applies also to the river Euphrates.

41.30.3.en: * What does he mean by the sea but the life of the lovers of the world, and what does he mean by the deep but their deep hidden thoughts? For this leviathan makes this deep sea boil like a pot, for it is very clear that in the last days of persecution he works to stir up the minds of the wicked against the elect with the flame of cruelty.

41.30.4.en: When ointments boil, a sweet fragrance comes from them. Leviathan will deceive the hearts of the wicked, so that whatever evil deeds of unbelief they do, they think they are doing them for the sake of truth and right faith.

41.30.6.en: What a deception of the wicked enemy! He stirs up the wicked who are like the sea and takes control of their hidden thoughts to urge them to resist the children of God by every means, and when they kill them they think they are offering service to God, as the Lord Christ Himself said (Jn 16:2).

41.30.7.en: Their depths boil with evil, and they think they are offering the ointments of truth with its sweet fragrance, in contrast to what the Lord Christ, the Truth, offers in the life of His children, that they may say with the Apostle Paul: "For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ" (2 Cor 2:15).

41.31.0.en: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary [32].

41.31.1.en: Because of the swiftness of his movement he leaves behind him white foam, as happens when swift ships pass through the waters. His traces look like the hair of an old gray-haired man.

41.31.2.en: Just as the Lord Christ makes His true believers "the light of the world," shining by Him on those around them to bring them into the kingdom of light, so the enemy deceives his followers. He appears as an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), and suggests to his followers that they know the truth and light the way, and that they have hidden wisdom, so that their bulk or their depths become like the gray-haired man of long experience and practical wisdom.

41.31.3.en: * Let no one be surprised at the heresies that exist today, for they have existed from the beginning, because Satan skillfully tries to mix falsehood with truth. And just as God from the beginning promised man many good things, so Satan always entices with his deceptive promises. God planted for them the garden of Eden, and Satan came and said to them: "Ye shall be as gods," and in fact he could not give them anything; all he did was dazzle them with his promises only. And this is what deceivers do.

41.32.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear [33].

41.32.1.en: In the Hebrew it reads "upon the mire." There is no animal like him, or the earth has not brought forth an animal so terrifying in its strength, violence, courage and ferocity. It is as if he were created so as not to fear or dread anyone.

41.32.2.en: Truly the devil has no equal on earth, and as Pope Gregory (the Great) says, although men know of his fall because of his deeds, yet he has not lost his angelic capabilities (his powers which he turned to evil), so he drew the human race and subjected it to himself. He boasts of the strength of his nature, by which he was able to rule over men.

41.32.3.en: * This is the enemy from whom we must flee. Who is this lion that follows us? St. Peter warns us and says to us: "Your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith" (1 Pet 5:8-9).

41.32.4.en: So there is a lion that has come up from his thicket: where then is this thicket? He fell down. He went down to the lowest parts of the earth, to its depths.

41.32.5.en: You are a man, you are higher than Satan, for in any case you are better than he. But he, because of his corruption, has gone down to the depths.

41.32.6.en: So if this lion comes out of his thicket, that is, from the place of his punishment (Hades), it will be said: "The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate" (Jer 4:7). He wants to enter your land, and wants to devour each one of us.

41.32.7.en: "Thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant. For this gird you with sackcloth" (b). Therefore, since the lion has come up to you to threaten you and to destroy your land, put on sackcloth, and weep and sigh and entreat God in prayers to destroy this lion and bring him to nothing so that you may be rid of him, and not fall between his teeth. For he tries to catch you through your ears, when he casts to you false words that are pleasing to your soul, to make you turn aside from the way of truth. And he wants also to devour your feet, and pull them away from the ground of truth. So be it! Gird yourself with sackcloth, and beat your breast, weep, and cry the cries of war when you see the enemy threatening you, that the fierceness of the Lord's anger may turn back from you, for you will have entered into the fortified city. Let us give thanks to God who delivers us in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory and might forever and ever, amen.

41.32.8.en: Origen He beholdeth all high things.

41.33.0.en: He is a king over all the children of pride [34].

41.33.1.en: He concludes his description by saying that in his arrogance he looks upon all the fierce and violent, haughty animals as less than himself, and oversees them as a king with authority; there is no animal that can resist him. All are subject to him, and he is subject to no one.

41.33.2.en: The lion is called the king of the forest or the king of the beasts; he is one of the children of pride, exalting himself by his power and capabilities. But before the animal mentioned here the lion loses his title.

41.33.3.en: * He looks down as one who is above all those who are beneath him. In his struggle against his Creator he disdains that anyone be reckoned like himself... In this it was well said by the prophet: "Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!" (Isa 5:21). So Paul says: "Be not wise in your own conceits" (Rom 12:16).

41.33.4.en: * "He is a king over all the children of pride." This leviathan, in order to fall in all the things mentioned before, struck himself with pride... He attacked the anointing of our immortality with the same weapon, as he destroyed his own blessed life. But God put this at the end of His discourse, for by pointing to the pride of this leviathan after mentioning all his evils, He indicates that it is the worst of all sins...

41.33.5.en: The man who exalts himself shamelessly in his mind, destruction quickly comes upon him. It is written: "Pride goeth before destruction" (Prov 16:18).

41.33.7.en: * We have fallen under the authority of our enemies - that is, "the god of this world" and his helpers from the powers of evil. As a result there arose our need of redemption by Him who buys us, so that we may return from the state of estrangement from Him. Therefore our Savior gave His blood as a ransom for us.... And since "the forgiveness of sins," which follows redemption, becomes impossible before man is set free, we must first be freed from the authority of him who took us captive and kept us under his control, and be freed from beyond the reach of his hand, so that we may obtain forgiveness of our sins and healing from the wounds of sin, so that we may accomplish works of godliness and other virtues.

41.33.8.en: *And truly; but if we prefer lust to God, sin reigns over us, for the Apostle says: "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body" (Rom 6:12).

41.33.9.en: So two kings strive to reign: sin or Satan reigns over the wicked, and righteousness or Christ reigns over the righteous.

41.33.10.en: Since the devil knew that Christ had come to seize his kingdom and subject to His power and authority those who had formerly been subject to the deceiver, he "shewed him all the kingdoms of the world" and all the inhabitants of the world; he showed Him how he reigns over one by lust, and over another by stinginess, over a third by love of vain glory, and takes others captive through the attraction of beauty... As if Satan were saying to Him: Do you want to reign over all creation?! And he showed Him the countless multitudes who are subject to him, and truly, if we accepted to know in simplicity our wretchedness and realize our calamity, we would find Satan reigning over most of the world; therefore the Lord calls him "the prince of this world" (Jn 12:31; 16:11). And when the devil says to Jesus: Do you see all the people subject to my authority? he has shown Him that "in a moment of time," for he reckons the present time a moment compared with eternity... Then the devil said to the Lord: Have you come to wrestle against me, and to take away from me all those who are under my authority? No, no, do not try to compare yourself with me, and do not expose yourself to the difficulties of this battle. See all that I ask of you, "If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine."

41.33.11.en: Without doubt our Lord and Savior wants to reign, but by justice and truth and every virtue... He does not want to be crowned as king without toil (the Cross)...

41.33.12.en: The Lord answered him, saying: [It is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve] (Deut 6:13) (c). My will is that all be Mine and worship Me, and not bow down to another. This is the royal desire. Would you have me sin, I who came to destroy sin and set men free from it?!

41.33.13.en: Let us rejoice and be glad, since we have become His, and let us pray to Him to kill the sin that reigned in our bodies (Rom 6:6), that He alone may reign over us.

41.33.15.en: By You I overcome him who overcame mankind!

41.33.16.en: * I have nothing to offer You but the sacrifice of praise, O Lover of all mankind!

41.33.17.en: You came into our world and clothed Yourself with our humanity, You became a true man, and the devil coveted You.

41.33.18.en: He thought You, like all men, would bow to him in humiliation.

41.33.19.en: * You offered him Your body as bait, and he leapt to devour it on the Cross.

41.33.20.en: The divine hook caught him, and he who thought himself king of the world became a plaything.

41.33.21.en: He fell into the snare, and his tongue was bound as with the cord of faith!

41.33.22.en: The little girls mocked him. He fell like lightning from the heaven of their hearts.

41.33.23.en: He was brought low to be under their feet.

41.33.24.en: He thought that by deceitful soft words he would escape from Your hand.

41.33.25.en: He confessed that You are the Holy One of God. And he realized that You had come to cast him out of his kingdom.

41.33.26.en: The enemy was confounded, but in his insolence he continued in his evil.

41.33.27.en: * By Your Cross You tore up my covenant with the enemy of good.

41.33.28.en: You freed me from him who thought he would enslave me eternally.

41.33.29.en: Instead of my humiliation before him, he has become humiliated. His resistance to me has not ceased, but it no longer crushes me. By You I overcome him who overcame mankind!

41.33.30.en: * I will no longer trust his promises.

41.33.31.en: I will not enter again into dialogue with him.

41.33.32.en: I will not waste my time with his words!

41.33.33.en: Your wonderful covenant with me is enough for me!

41.33.34.en: You gave it to me written with Your blood on the Cross.

41.33.35.en: * In his deceit he comes to me wherever I am.

41.33.36.en: On the land I see him eating grass like the ox.

41.33.37.en: And in the sea I see him swimming like the crocodile.

41.33.38.en: And in the air he appears like a bird soaring to the heights!

41.33.39.en: He uses every means to join me to himself.

41.33.40.en: He stirs up passions so that man may find pleasure in them.

41.33.41.en: And he breathes the spirit of pride to puff up the believer with his own righteousness.

41.33.42.en: He appears as a lion to terrify those who look at him.

41.33.43.en: And he appears as an angel of light to deceive the believers.

41.33.44.en: * He binds the wicked to himself like the scales of a crocodile.

41.33.45.en: Each unites with the rest to form a solid, closely bound company.

41.33.46.en: They have no work but to add new scales every day.

41.33.47.en: Their consciences are quieted since all work together.

41.33.48.en: By their union together they let none of them slip out of their hands.

41.33.49.en: For they do not allow the breath of holy counsel to penetrate them.

41.33.50.en: * The enemy breathes out the evil of his pride from his nose.

41.33.51.en: And deceptive lamps come forth from his mouth.

41.33.52.en: He fills the air with the smoke of deception by his false miracles.

41.33.53.en: And he creeps into the minds of the corrupt with his false light.

41.33.54.en: * He breathes fire upon the minds of the wicked, and makes it a destructive fire, inflaming wicked pleasures in them.

41.33.55.en: He exalts himself with his stretched-out neck like one in authority.

41.33.56.en: He breathes the spirit of hatred and loathing into the world, and so turns the hearts of many into stones bearing the marks of his cruelty.

41.33.57.en: * How marvelous, for his war against the Church does not cease. He wants to turn iron souls into worthless straw, and hearts hard as brass into feeble wood.

41.33.58.en: He concentrates his blows on the preachers of the truth, and directs his swords and spears against those who labor in the Lord's vineyard.

41.33.59.en: He did not learn from the battle of the Cross.

41.33.60.en: For by the Cross children became heroic soldiers, and the arrows of his bow turned into feeble stubble!

41.33.61.en: * What folly of the devil! He has not learned from the lesson of the Cross!

41.33.62.en: In stubbornness he urges his wicked children to persecute the children of God.

41.33.63.en: He controls their hidden thoughts and deceives them.

41.33.64.en: And while they kill the righteous, they think they are serving God.

41.33.65.en: And while they resist the truth they reckon themselves to be bearing the sweet fragrance of truth.

41.33.66.en: * He throws the believers on the anvil, and strikes them with all his strength with the hammer, thinking he is able to shape them to become in his likeness.

41.33.67.en: The Crucified One does not prevent him from striking, but turns his hammer into powerless straw!

41.33.68.en: And his trials become a cause of victory and crowns of glory for the children of God.
